findings: The prompt trades away single high-contradiction boundaries by downranking them, then prefers alternative cuts that fragment noun phrases or enumerations—this consistently harms short-latency (≤3 and ≤5) cases.
The prompt under-specifies predicate completion: it allows cuts that separate verbs/predicates from their core arguments or complements, producing contradicted or fragmentary pieces.

diagnosis.why: Replacing several examples with short‑latency NP/enumeration cases taught the scorer to avoid cutting inside tiny lists/NPs (explaining the small gain in the ≤3 bin), but it overgeneralized: in mid‑latency ranges (≤5 and ≤10) the scorer shifted cuts toward predicate/argument boundaries and inserted extra micro‑cuts, producing more fragmentation and a net small drop in H_set.
diagnosis.lesson: Keep examples that discourage fragmenting very short lists/NPs, but ensure those examples don't cause the scorer to relocate cuts into predicate/argument boundaries or create many tiny fragments in mid‑latency items.
